subject: Topology & egress contract alignment for Helion private deployment
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@helionfinance.com>, devops@helionfinance.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Topology & egress contract alignment for Helion private deployment

Hi Daniel / Helion infra team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. I attached a first-pass egress contract PDF and an annotated topology (vpc-topology-annotated.png) to make the questions concrete. Short version of what we need to confirm before the control/data plane cutover: 

- Control plane traffic: Redwood control plane (management API, rotation/auth callbacks, metrics ingestion) will originate from our control-plane bastion IPs in the hosted control region and must be able to reach Helion's management VLAN 10.
- Data plane: inference traffic stays within the customer VPC and to on-prem inference nodes; we only expect TLS-terminated connections to our runtime sidecars.
- Egress constraints: Helion wants to restrict outbound connections; we need a minimum allowlist for endpoints (keys rotation, metrics, model pull).

Questions:
1) Can Helion permit outbound TLS (443) from the sidecar/worker subnet to these hostnames/IP ranges in the draft? (list in attached PDF)
2) Is there a preferred proxy pattern you want? (explicit egress NAT + perimeter proxy, or a cluster sidecar egress enforced via firewall rules)
3) Any IDS/IPS or TLS inspection that would break mTLS/our signed cert exchange for model pulls?

Action requested: please review the attached draft and reply with the preferred egress enforcement approach and any additional allowlist entries. If helpful, we can sketch an alternate topology with an edge proxy in front of sidecars.

Attachments: 20260909-helion-egress-draft.pdf, vpc-topology-annotated.png

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Private Deploy 
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

---
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@helionfinance.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@helionfinance.com
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Topology & egress contract alignment for Helion private deployment

Mina — thanks for the clear doc. Quick answers inline: 

1) Allowlist: We can approve outbound 443 to the hostnames in your draft, plus our proxy list (see note). Please also include our internal artifact registry (10.14.3.8) — we mirror model artifacts there for audit.
2) Proxy pattern: At Helion we prefer a single egress proxy cluster (north-south) per datacenter for audit/IDS. Sidecars are supported but extra config is required. If Redwood needs connection pooling/keepalive to improve latency we can open internal bypass for sidecar->sidecar to reduce hop count.
3) TLS inspection: We do have TLS inspection for outbound to external hosts. For the model pull path we can create an inspection-allowlist for your mTLS cert chain if you provide cert fingerprints ahead of time.

We can accommodate the changes but need a final list of endpoints and a short runbook for failback in case the proxy denies flows during cutover.

—Daniel
Principal Infra Eng, Helion Finance

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@helionfinance.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Topology & egress contract alignment for Helion private deployment

Looping in ops/infra notes and a recommended fallback:

- Recommendation: Adopt Helion's perimeter egress proxy as primary for audit. Configure our runtime sidecars to use a local proxy stub (localhost:3129) that routes to the perimeter proxy. This gives Helion a single audit point and allows sidecars to keep TCP keepalive to reduce token-latency churn.
- Observability: we'll emit a short-lived request-id header on each model-pull and metrics push. Irene, can we add a manifest of fingerprints (sha256) for the model-fetch cert chain into the drive link?
- Failback plan: If the perimeter proxy blocks flows during canary, we will immediately open an alternate direct egress route to our control-plane bastions (policy-controlled, ticketed) so the canary can continue while debugging the proxy rules.

Attachments: snippet of canary runbook (Confluence link below).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — great notes. Action items consolidated below with owners and timeline: 

1) Mina / Redwood (today EOD PST): post cert fingerprints (sha256) for model-pull chain and update the Drive doc. (related link in metadata)
2) Daniel / Helion (tomorrow): confirm the perimeter proxy allowlist and add Helion's artifact mirror 10.14.3.8 to our PDF draft.
3) Irene / Redwood (tomorrow AM): produce a short fallback runbook (steps, tickets, rollback criteria) and attach to the Confluence runbook.
4) Marissa / Redwood (pre-cutover): validate canary traffic shape and confirm keepalive parameters that Helion's proxy will preserve.

Please confirm if timelines look feasible. If Helion prefers we can sketch a small alternate diagram that places an edge-proxy stub for the sidecars — this may reduce TLS inspection friction.

Attachments: updated 20260909-helion-egress-draft.pdf (v2 will include artifact mirror and fingerprint table)

Thanks,
Mina
